narration.text: One green leaf. Somewhere out there, something was growing again. And when Noah held it, he knew: the waters were really going.
Eight people who had not smiled in months passed that leaf from hand to hand like treasure. A single leaf. It was the first word of the new world.
And he stayed yet other seven days; and sent forth the dove; which returned not again unto him any more.
Seven days later he sent her out one last time. And she never came back. That silence was the best news of all: the dove had found a home.

And it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dry.
Dry ground at last, right before his eyes. And still the door stayed shut. The One who closed it had not yet said open.

publish_decision.note: Defect list of local review 41639836811 and the frame sheet of this exact master (sha256 b1ab37e9...): no speech cut off (0.25 s clear on both sides; first words 'One green leaf', last 'had not yet said open'), pictures fit the lines (the dove with the leaf, the family sharing it, Noah releasing the dove, Noah at the window looking at dry ground), no audio error (-14.1 LUFS, true peak -1.5 dBTP, no silence inside speech), no policy issue. Peak is the first scene change at 9 s from the dove close-up to the family: the emotional peak is 'passed that leaf from hand to hand like treasure'. It ends on an open loop: the door stays shut until God says open, which the long answers. Range 235.54-298.77 s is inside no other cut or reflection clip of the long beyond the fade margin (E279).
